answers.question: Why does my Canon T5i with the EF-S 18-55 IS STM hunt for focus?

verdict.headline: Your T5i and EF-S 18-55 IS STM are manufacturer-covered for smooth Movie Servo AF, but focus hunting is usually from difficult AF subjects/lighting, Live View or video AF behavior, or the camera choosing the wrong target.

findings.point: Canon records a Live View focus caveat for the T5i: low contrast, low light, repetitive patterns, and moving subjects can make the camera hunt or fail to lock. Canon, page 165.
findings.quote: Shooting conditions that make focusing difficult

source.title: EOS REBEL T5i / EOS 700D Instruction Manual

findings.point: The knowledge base summarizes the T5i manual as saying Live View uses contrast-detect or hybrid AF for most methods, which is slower than viewfinder phase-detect AF. Difficult cases include low contrast, low light, repetitive patterns, fine lines, moving subjects, very small subjects, edge-of-frame subjects, reflective subjects, and mixed near/far subjects inside one AF point.

modes.remedy: Use FlexiZone-Single and place the AF point on a clear edge or the subject’s eye; add light or choose a higher-contrast target. For Live View stills, try Quick mode for faster phase-detect focusing, or switch the lens to MF if AF will not lock.

findings.point: Canon records that the T5i viewfinder AF can fail on certain difficult subjects such as very low contrast, very low light, strong backlight, reflective subjects, near/far overlap, or repetitive patterns. Canon, page 103.
findings.quote: Autofocus can fail to achieve focus (viewfinder’s focus confirmation light <o> blinks) with certain subjects such as the following:

source.title: EOS REBEL T5i / EOS 700D Instruction Manual

findings.point: If you are in Basic Zone auto modes, Canon says the camera normally focuses the closest subject, so it may not focus the subject you intended. Canon, page 100.
findings.quote: In Basic Zone modes, the camera will normally focus the closest subject automatically. Therefore, it may not always focus your target subject.

source.title: EOS REBEL T5i / EOS 700D Instruction Manual

findings.point: The knowledge base summarizes the T5i viewfinder AF as a 9-point phase-detect system. For still subjects, One-Shot locks focus; for motion, AI Servo keeps adjusting. Manual AF-point selection in Creative Zone modes lets you tell the camera exactly where to focus.

modes.remedy: Use P, Tv, Av, or M instead of full auto; manually select an AF point, preferably over a high-contrast part of the subject. For a still subject, use One-Shot AF, lock focus, and recompose. If it still cannot lock, focus on another object at the same distance or switch the lens to MF.

findings.point: Canon lists the EF-S 18-55 IS STM Movie Servo AF function as compatible with the EOS Rebel T5i/700D. Canon, page 2.
findings.quote: Function compatible with the following camera (as of June 2013): EOS REBEL T5i/700D, EOS REBEL SL1/100D, EOS REBEL T4i/650D, EOS M (when using with Mount Adapter EF-EOS M)

findings.point: The knowledge base summarizes Canon’s movie guidance: Movie Servo AF continuously focuses, but fast subjects moving toward or away from the camera, close subjects, panning, zooming, or magnification can make focus momentarily shift or stop.

The knowledge base summarizes the STM lens behavior: the EF-S 18-55 IS STM is designed for quiet, smooth Movie Servo AF on compatible bodies like the T5i, but it is still an electronic focus-by-wire system rather than a direct mechanical focusing ring.

modes.remedy: For video, use Movie Servo AF only when you need continuous tracking. If the camera keeps breathing or hunting, pause or disable Movie Servo AF, pre-focus, use FlexiZone-Single on the subject, add light/contrast, or focus manually for the shot.

findings.point: One lens-specific caveat is not hunting, but can look like a focus problem: the STM lens cannot be manually focused electronically when the camera is off. Canon, page 7.
findings.quote: Manual focus adjustments are not possible when the camera is OFF.

findings.point: The knowledge base summarizes that this STM lens also enters sleep behavior; if the camera or lens has slept, half-pressing the shutter wakes it before focusing normally.

modes.remedy: If the lens seems unresponsive, half-press the shutter to wake it, wait a moment after power-on, and make sure the lens switch is set to AF for autofocus or MF for manual focus.

answers.question: Sigma 35mm F1.4 Art on a Sony a7 IV through the MC-11: AF-C and DMF?

verdict.headline: Yes for AF-S, but no for AF-C and no for DMF with the Sigma 35mm F1.4 DG HSM Art on the Sony a7 IV through the Sigma MC-11.

findings.point: Sigma’s MC-11 lens table for the 35mm F1.4 DG HSM Art shows AF-S supported, AFC/AFA not supported, and DMF not supported; Sigma, page 1.

source.title: MC-11 lens compatibility table, row: Lens | AFS | AFC/AFA | DMF (○ supported, × not supported)

findings.point: Sigma also states globally for the MC-11 that the camera’s AF-C is not supported; Sigma, page 1.
findings.quote: The camera's AF-C is not supported.

findings.point: The knowledge-base summary lists α7IV among Sigma’s checked Sony E-mount bodies for the MC-11 and summarizes the same restrictions: AF-C/AFA unsupported, and this 35mm Art row has DMF marked unsupported.

modes.remedy: Use AF-S for stills. Do not expect AF-C tracking or DMF with this lens on the MC-11; switch to manual focus when you need manual override, or use a native E-mount lens/combination with AF-C and DMF support.

answers.question: Canon EF 50mm f/1.8 II on a Sony body with the Metabones Mark V

verdict.headline: Covered, but it is not a clean yes: Metabones lists the EF 50mm f/1.8 II as potentially inaccurate, and continuous AF depends on the Sony body generation and adapter mode.

modes.condition: Canon EF 50mm f/1.8 II on Metabones EF-to-Sony E Mark V; best case requires a PDAF-capable camera

findings.point: Metabones specifically lists this lens, but warns that autofocus may not be accurate even if it may be usable on a phase-detect AF camera.
findings.quote: AF may not be accurate, but may be usable on a camera with PDAF (GH7, OM-1. etc.)

findings.point: The lens is a micro-motor EF lens; the knowledge base summarizes that conventional micro-motor AF is mechanical, unlike STM designs that are optimized for smoother movie servo behavior.

modes.remedy: Use a Sony body with phase-detect AF if possible, and do not treat AF accuracy as guaranteed; check critical focus and be ready to use manual focus.

modes.condition: Sony bodies from 2014 or earlier, or without phase-detect AF, such as A7S II

findings.point: For older Sony bodies or bodies without phase-detect AF, Metabones says AF-S is the safer mode and AF-C may hunt or be inaccurate.
findings.quote: AF-C may have unsatisfactory performance and/or accuracy and may suffer from excessive hunting, depending on lens - use AF-S or DMF

findings.point: The EF 50mm f/1.8 II has an additional lens-specific warning that AF may not be accurate.
findings.quote: AF may not be accurate, but may be usable on a camera with PDAF (GH7, OM-1. etc.)

modes.remedy: Use AF-S or DMF rather than AF-C on these bodies; switch to manual focus if hunting or missed focus continues.

modes.condition: Sony bodies from 2015 on with phase-detect AF, adapter in Advanced mode

findings.point: Metabones states that continuous video AF is supported on phase-detect AF supported cameras when using the adapter’s Advanced mode condition recorded here.
findings.quote: Continuous video AF with phase-detection AF on supported cameras

findings.point: The lens-specific listing still warns that autofocus accuracy is not guaranteed.
findings.quote: AF may not be accurate, but may be usable on a camera with PDAF (GH7, OM-1. etc.)

modes.remedy: For video continuous AF, use a 2015-or-newer Sony body with phase-detect AF and put the Metabones Mark V in Advanced mode; test before relying on it for critical takes.

answers.question: Nikon AF-S 50mm f/1.8G on a Canon EOS R6 with an F-to-RF adapter

verdict.headline: No manufacturer record in this dataset covers the Nikon AF-S 50mm f/1.8G on a Canon EOS R6 with an F-to-RF adapter.
verdict.notCoveredReason: The dataset lookup did not find a Canon EOS R6 body record, a Nikon AF-S 50mm f/1.8G lens record, or an F-to-RF adapter record, so there is no applicable manufacturer compatibility record for this combination.

findings.point: No matching manufacturer compatibility record or focus caveat was found for this body/lens/adapter combination in the dataset.
Because the adapter is not covered, I cannot infer autofocus just because a physical F-to-RF adapter may fit.

modes.remedy: Use a manufacturer-documented electronic adapter/lens/body combination, or treat this setup as not verified for autofocus by this dataset and be prepared to focus manually.
